sets.relationshipLabel: device and the component it always carries
sets.explanation: A camera without a lens or a projector without a lamp can't do its job — each device inherently carries this part.

sets.relationshipLabel: moments bracketing a span of filmmaking
sets.explanation: Opening and closing credits bookend a screening just as greenlight and wrap bookend a production.

sets.relationshipLabel: subject and the made image that stands for it
sets.explanation: A poster represents a film the same way a headshot represents a star — each is the image made to stand in for the real thing.

sets.relationshipLabel: safeguard that stops a specific harm
sets.explanation: A stunt double exists to prevent injury, and a completion bond exists to prevent a shutdown — each is a safeguard tied to one specific risk.

glossary.definition: A financial guarantee that pays back backers if money runs out before a job is finished.

definitions.definition: The device that captures the moving images you end up watching.
The curved glass piece that focuses light so you get a sharp picture.
A machine that throws a bright picture up onto a big screen.
The bright bulb inside that makes the picture on screen glow.
The names and titles that roll at the very start of a show.
The scrolling list of names that plays after the story ends.
The official go-ahead that lets a project start being made.
The moment when filming is officially declared finished.
A movie — the finished story you watch from start to end.
A big printed image made to advertise something and pull people in.
The famous lead performer everyone's excited to see.
A close-up photo of someone's face used to show who they are.
A skilled performer who steps in for the risky physical action.
Physical harm someone might suffer, especially during dangerous work.
A financial guarantee that pays back backers if money runs out before a job is finished.
A sudden stop that halts a whole operation before it's done.
